pages.text: $(thing)Portable engines$() have had two major changes in $(#f80051)TerraFirmaNautics$():$(li)Their $(bold)recipe$() has been changed to be much more complex and require $(l:mechanics/steel)advanced materials$(), given the $(thing)portable engine$() is a near limitless source of rotational power.$(li)Pipes and pumps cand now be used to feed liquid fuels to the $(thing)portable engines$().
The crafting recipe now requires, among other things, $(l:mechanics/steel)steel$() and $(thing)electrum$().

$(thing)Liquid fuels$() can be pumped into the portable engine, and are a $(bold)more efficient$() replacement of traditional solid fuels.$(br)The more popular $(o)solid fuels$() are:$(li)$(bold)Charcoal$() burns for 2:05.$(li)$(bold)Lignite$() burns for 2:30.$(li)$(bold)Bituminous coal$() burns for 5:30.$(br)The main $(o)liquid fuels$() are:$(li)$(bold)Lava$() burns for 16:40.$(li)$(bold)Biofuel$() burns for 12:30.$(li)$(bold)Olive oil$() burns for 8:20.$(li)$(bold)Canola oil$() burns for 8:20.$(li)$(bold)Soybean oil$() burns for 8:20.$(li)$(bold)Seed oil$() burns for 5:50.

pages.title: Liquid fuels
pages.text: While very efficient, liquid fuels $(bold)must$() be piped into the $(thing)portable engine$(), you can't just pour them in with a bucket and expect the fuel to not mess with the engine's delicate internal machinery.
